title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 35
paragraphs: At that time in Athens the government was held by Peisistratus, but Miltiades son of Cypselus also had some power. He belonged to a family that kept four-horse chariot teams, and was descended originally from Aeacus and Aegina, though in more recent times his family was Athenian, Philaeus son of Ajax being the first of his house to become an Athenian. This Miltiades was sitting in the entrance of his own house, and seeing the Dolonkians passing by in clothing that was not of the native Athenian fashion and carrying spears, he called out to them; and when they approached, he offered them lodging and hospitality. They accepted, and after being entertained by him they declared to him all the utterances of the oracle; and having declared it, they asked him to do as the god had said. Miltiades, when he heard it, was at once disposed to agree, because he was vexed by Peisistratus's rule and desired to be out of the way. So he set off at once to Delphi to inquire of the oracle whether he should do what the Dolonkians were asking of him.
